This time, I’m taking things seriously: a new domain, a new platform and a personal investment that I intend to keep up over the long term.
I’ve looked into how I could support the site and make it self-sustaining, so I can focus on creating content.
I don’t really like advertising through banners (Google AdSense), either for its appearance or as a concept, so I haven’t considered it for now. Instead, I’ve decided to try Buy Me a Coffee, a platform that lets readers support creators with a small, voluntary contribution. The amount is entirely up to you, and there’s no obligation. It would be lovely to eventually cover the site’s costs through this kind of support and perhaps offer other types of content on other platforms.
That’s all for now. Thanks in advance to anyone who chooses to make a small contribution to keep the blog online.

content:
As Aldo would say: “I can’t believe it!” And yes, on 12 January 2027, I’ll celebrate 20 years since arriving here in Australia.
I still remember it as if it were yesterday—well, if I’m honest, not quite—but I’ll try to tell you about it.
I arrived in Brisbane with plenty of ideas, dreams to pursue and a new life to plan.
It certainly wasn’t easy. There were many sacrifices to make and decisions to take, without a deep understanding of Australian institutions or familiar faces I could turn to for advice. But I had a solid plan: I was on the other side of the world to reinvent myself, and my first goal was to try to obtain citizenship. Eligibility was based on a points system calculated from factors such as education, age and work experience.
I admit I had moments of discouragement, but in the end I never gave up. With the stubbornness of a true Bergamasco, I got there. I still had to graduate, complete another year of study through the ACS (Australian Computer Society) and do an internship. After that, I had enough points to apply for citizenship.
I’ll leave it there for now, but I’ll come back to this topic later.

Welcome once again to my personal blog. This space on the web will share a little about my life here in Australia. I’m building it with Hugo, one of the most popular open-source static site generators. For the theme, I chose PaperMod. I like its clean style and lack of unnecessary frills.
From ChatGPT:
Static sites, such as those built with Hugo, offer many advantages over traditional CMS platforms like WordPress. Because they’re generated directly as HTML, CSS and JavaScript, they deliver high performance, very fast load times and a smoother browsing experience. They don’t require a database or server-side processing, which also makes them more secure, less exposed to attacks and easier to maintain. They’re also easy to version and manage with Git, and can be published automatically using tools such as GitHub Actions. The result is a modern, lightweight, scalable and affordable solution—ideal for anyone who wants a fast, reliable website that’s easy to maintain.

content:
How about you? Unless a movie is especially gripping, I often find it too long to watch in one evening. I don’t always make it to the end and end up falling asleep on the couch. Thankfully, there are wonderful TV series, which I love and find much easier to watch after a long day.
I especially enjoy science fiction, spy dramas, and crime series (British ones are best). Every now and then, I also watch something lighter, just for a change.
Genre: science fiction This week, I finished the third season of Silo. After a somewhat heavy-going second season, I thought this latest one was incredible: it clarified many details and events from earlier seasons, which finally make sense. For me, it was a fantastic season! Now we wait for the fourth, due to arrive on July 9, 2027, on Apple’s streaming platform. Watch the trailer.
More recommendations Battlestar Galactica — A little dated, but a must-watch for science-fiction fans. Watch the trailer. For All Mankind — A great series now in its fifth season, with one final season expected next year to wrap up the story. It presents an alternate reality where the space race and rivalry between superpowers take a different course. It’s also available on Apple’s streaming platform. Watch the trailer. Foundation — A great series now in its third season. The storyline is quite complex, so I’ll let you discover it for yourself. Available on Apple’s streaming platform. Watch the trailer. Honorable mention Severance — A very unusual series, sometimes a little slow but fascinating in its concept. A procedure separates a person’s work memories from their personal ones, creating two distinct identities for each employee: the “innie,” who knows nothing about the outside world, and the “outie,” who lives outside work without knowing anything about their job. Available on Apple’s streaming platform. Watch the trailer. Upload — Set in 2033, Upload imagines a future where people can “upload” their consciousness to a digital afterlife when their bodies die. The experience can be more or less ideal, depending on how much they pay. Available on Hulu. Watch the trailer. Have a TV series to recommend? Send me a message via the Contact page; I’d love to hear your suggestions.

Hi, I’m Vanni, the owner and author of iBloggy.net.
This is a little corner of the internet where I share my life in Australia as an expat.
My wife and I thought it would be nice to use this space to collect and share all the moments that make our journey exciting, sometimes challenging, but always meaningful.
From renovating our home to the ups and downs of everyday life, iBloggy is where we gather the stories that shape our experience in Australia and connect with anyone who would like to follow us on this journey.
Technology used This blog was built with Hugo, one of the most popular open-source static site generators. I could have used WordPress or another CMS with all sorts of plugins and bells and whistles, but as they say, “less is more”. The beauty of a static site like this, built with Hugo, is its speed, simplicity and, above all, security, as there is no database to manage.
If you’d like to support the website, consider making a small donation. I’ll enjoy a good cup of coffee in your honour! Just click the yellow button below. And, most importantly, thank you from the bottom of my heart.
title: About

content:
This personal blog is hosted using GitHub Pages. When you visit the site, GitHub may process and log your IP address for security purposes. For more information, see GitHub’s Privacy Statement.
This site uses Cloudflare Web Analytics to measure page views and page performance. The beacon sends navigation and timing metrics to Cloudflare. Cloudflare states that Web Analytics does not collect or use visitors’ personal data and does not track end users across its customers’ websites. For details, see its information on data collection and Cloudflare Web Analytics.
Comments on blog posts are provided by EchoThread. Loading the widget connects your browser to EchoThread’s CDN. If you submit a comment, EchoThread receives the comment and technical data, including your IP address and user-agent, for moderation and abuse prevention. It may also receive profile details you provide or use to sign in. Published comments are public. See EchoThread’s Privacy Policy.
This site does not use advertising services. Every page also loads the Buy Me a Coffee button script from its CDN; this connection may involve processing technical data such as your IP address. If you interact with the button, Buy Me a Coffee’s privacy practices apply.
If you send a message through the contact form, the details you enter are sent to Web3Forms so they can forward them to me by email. Web3Forms says it processes data on servers in the United States. See Web3Forms’ privacy information.
Search runs in your browser; your search terms are not sent to me. External links lead to websites with their own privacy policies.
This notice may be updated if the site’s features change.
